concept.name: Color
concept.definition: Color is a third-order sensitivity of an option's value: the rate of change of gamma with the passage of time, equivalently the third derivative of value with respect to the underlying price (twice) and time (once). It measures how a position's convexity profile decays as expiration approaches.
concept.intuition: Color tells you how fast your gamma is aging: near expiration, the gamma of at-the-money options swells while out-of-the-money gamma withers, changing your hedge needs day by day.
concept.mechanics: Color = d(gamma)/d(tau) = d3V/(dS2 d(tau)), often quoted as gamma change per day. It is monitored by traders maintaining gamma-hedged books, because the hedge adjustment schedule depends on how gamma itself evolves; near expiry, color itself changes rapidly, degrading full-day estimates.
concept.failure_modes: Color is a fine-grained model derivative whose practical estimates are noisy: input errors in volatility and time are amplified at third order, and near expiration its own instability makes day-ahead hedge forecasts unreliable.
concept.misconceptions: Color is not the time decay of the option's price (theta) or of its delta (charm) — it is the time decay of gamma, a distinction that matters only for books actively managing convexity.
concept.example: A 10-day ATM option's gamma might rise from 0.05 to 0.09 over the final week; a color reading of +0.004 per day warns the gamma hedger that re-hedge frequency must increase into expiry.
